facebook.content_angle: Breathing pattern optimisation — how most club swimmers default to every-stroke breathing and bleed speed, versus the controlled bilateral and reduced breathing patterns elite swimmers use to maintain power through fatigue
facebook.post_text:
Your breathing pattern is costing you seconds. 💨

Most club swimmers breathe every stroke, every lap — without thinking. It feels comfortable. But comfort doesn't win races.

Here's what fast swimmers do differently:
👉 They practise reduced breathing sets (every 3, 5, or 7 strokes) to train CO2 tolerance
👉 They shift to bilateral breathing in training to balance stroke mechanics and fix body roll asymmetry
👉 They pre-plan their race breathing pattern — and execute it under pressure, not on instinct

The swimmers who control their breath control the race. 🔥

✔️ Try this: 10 x 50m — breathe every 3 strokes for the first 25m, then hold every 5 for the back half
✔️ Track how your stroke feels when oxygen is a resource you manage, not a reflex
✔️ Do this consistently for four weeks and your race composure will be unrecognisable

What's your current breathing pattern in races — do you stick to a plan or just go with what feels right?
